channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Financial Times] Musk sets lower sales target for Tesla as it explores SpaceX merger
item.description: Carmaker reports flat revenue and falling profits as it pivots from electric vehicles to AI

item.title: [Financial Times] Meta agrees deal to keep Zuckerberg in California despite wealth tax proposal
item.description: Group to create new class of non-voting shares to allow stock sales without diluting founder’s control

item.title: [EU Observer] EU prosecutors raid far-right Patriots for Europe offices in Brussels and Strasbourg over alleged misuse of parliament funds
item.description: The European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) raided the offices of Patriots for Europe in Strasbourg and Brussels.

item.title: [DW] Trump, Putin and Xi at one table, without Ukraine. What Moscow wants from the proposal and why Beijing might agree.
item.description: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, without Kyiv or the EU. What does Russia hope to gain, and why might China be willing to take part?

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Project Fear’ didn’t work, so why do we keep demonising far-right and left voters?
item.description: My beef with both far-right and far-left populists is that they're false prophets. In Europe, at least, the squeezes on public services, high taxes, debt burdens and crippling costs of living are legacies of the Covid pandemic, wars in Ukraine and Iran and a eurozone crisis that was never fully resolved. These can’t be wished away, and they won’t be cured with caps on immigration, higher taxes on the

item.title: [DW] Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
item.description: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity" between the two.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU looks to UK, Canada, and Japan to plug €70bn hole in funding for Ukraine’s 2027 war effort
item.description: The EU is pressing allies, such as the UK, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Australia, and Norway to help close a €70bn shortfall in Ukraine’s funding for next year.

item.title: [EU Observer] Human cost of Putin’s war emerging in ‘death fields’ of Russian soldiers in Dobropillia (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,700)
item.description: Moscow has concentrated its biggest force near Pokrovsk and faked new front lines on paper. Meanwwhile, the real battle around Dobropillia is reshaping how Europe must think about any ceasefire, which could lock in Russian gains

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘I hear MEPs say Muslims are a threat, with no consequences. I say Free Palestine and I’ll be arrested’ – MEP Benedetta Scuderi warns protest repression is being normalised in Europe
item.description: Defending human and environmental rights could get you in prison, or at least detained - as happened to Italian MEP Benedetta Scuderi. She talks to EUobserver about the double-standard in policing of left and rightwing demos, and the housing crisis sparking much of the youth unrest.

item.title: [DW] Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
item.description: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.

item.title: [DW] Russia frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff talks
item.description: During talks between Vladimir Putin and Steve Witkoff, Putin announced that jailed American Stephen Hubbard had been released. The Kremlin also said Russia was "in principle" ready to resume trilateral talks next month.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s youth asked for hope – but politicians just offer fear and hate
item.description: As Europe pours billions into defence and talks up ‘strategic autonomy’, it is quietly undermining its own power by ignoring the students who say they can’t afford the education, housing or stability needed to keep the continent running.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘I’m 42 and I’ve spent my entire adult life held captive by Bibi’ – can Israel finally break free of Netanyahu, as Hungary did of Orbán?
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu has not been Israel’s prime minister for every one of those years. Yet even out of office, Israeli politics rarely escaped his gravitational pull. Hungarians know something about that feeling.

item.title: [DW] UK fighter jets to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
item.description: The UK is sending military support to Saudi Arabia as Iran-aligned Houthi rebels launch repeated attacks on the kingdom.

item.title: [DW] Portugal housing protests continue after police clear camps
item.description: Demonstrators vow to continue their campaign to call for affordable housing in Portugal after police cleared tent camps and arrested at least 55 people.

item.title: [EU Observer] The US is no longer an ally. It’s over.
item.description: Even an eventual change of American leadership doesn't mean the US's bizarre glorification of violence goes away. It is a persistent stain, constantly eroding away at the values of an open and free society. Both are worth defending here in Europe. The US has chosen its own path. Let it walk it alone.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU unlikely to send Black Sea naval mission to repel Russian drone attacks on Ukrainian grain ships, despite Kallas’ support
item.description: The EU's top diplomat has backed the idea of a Black Sea naval mission to protect grain ships from Russian drones - but this would require much more than Europe's existing Red Sea operation, while air policing might be more effective.

item.title: [DW] New EU plan for Arctic warily eyes influence of Russia, US
item.description: The EU unveiled its priorities in the Arctic as it vies with Russia, China and the US for influence. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said drone incursions, GPS jamming and cable sabotage undermine Arctic security.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs push to use EU regional funds for affordable housing and climate‑proofing cities
item.description: The European Parliament called on more spending to build affordable houses, using funds for regional development that currently comprise up to a third of the present EU budget.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs open arms to UK rejoining EU to ‘correct’ Brexit mistake
item.description: Members of European Parliament from across the political spectrum are holding the door open for Britain to rejoin the union.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU vows to stop buying Arctic oil and gas, but drops ban from its new strategy
item.description: EU officials vowed an end to Arctic oil and gas buying, as the European Commission presented its new Arctic strategy. But while the document commits to keeping Arctic oil and gas “in the ground,” it drops the call for an international ban.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukrainians evacuate soldier using heavy air drone after he spent 500 days at the front, in another first-ever in the war (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,699)
item.description: While US secretary of state Marco Rubio publicly echoes Vladimir Putin’s inflated claims about Russian gains in Donetsk, Ukrainian crews on the ground are using scarce drones to snatch back their own wounded from territory Moscow says it controls.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s €800bn defence borrowing hides a reality of every country buying on its own
item.description: In defence, the bigger the order, the longer the production line and the lower the cost of each unit. That is a big reason why Europe has long bought American, for price as much as for technology. Europe could match it by buying together and sharing out the work along the value chain.

item.title: [Financial Times] Global stocks tumble as oil prices rise
item.description: China’s CSI 300 index sheds 1.8% and Eurozone bond sell-off deepens

item.title: [EU Observer] Polish parliament liberalises abortion law – but conservative president likely to veto changes
item.description: The Polish governing coalition voted in parliament to loosen abortion law on Tuesday - but conservative president is expected to block the change.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign
item.description: Bulgaria's presidential election campaign has been shaped by recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea and the government's lack of support for Ukraine, making foreign policy a key factor in the first round.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Adipositas: Sparen kann für den Staat teuer werden
item.description: Adipositas wird in Deutschland vor allem als medizinisches oder individuelles Problem diskutiert. Doch die Erkrankung hat erhebliche wirtschaftliche Folgen. Der Blick ins Ausland zeigt, dass die politische Debatte über die Versorgung von Adipositas auch anders geführt werden kann.

item.description: Künstliche Intelligenz verschärft die Bedrohungslage für Unternehmen und stellt klassische Schutzkonzepte auf die Probe. Wie sich IT-Systeme dennoch wirksam und rund um die Uhr schützen lassen, zeigt Babor mit innovativen Sicherheitslösungen.

item.description: Czech President Petr Pavel said the U.S. diesel deal with Russia gives Moscow “new hope.”

item.title: [DW] France: Young voters blase about Glucksmann's Socialists
item.description: Raphael Glucksmann wants to lead France's Socialists to power without working with the left-populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, who is particularly popular with young voters. How can the center-left candidate win them over?

item.title: [DW] How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service?
item.description: Kyiv keeps issuing warnings that the satellite internet system Starlink is being restricted in Ukraine. How dependent is the country on the system, and what would happen if it went down?

item.title: [DW] Populist Czech PM Babis goes empty-handed in Senate elections
item.description: Opposition parties still control the Czech Senate, in a major blow to Prime Minister Andrej Babis' and his governing coalition.

item.title: [DW] Russia wants blackout in Ukraine as winter comes — Zelenskyy
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says Russia is trying to cut electricity and heating to civilians ahead of winter. He also called the US president's waiver of new sanctions on Moscow a boost for Vladimir Putin.

item.title: [DW] France: Protesters clash with police in nationwide protests, amid rising social polarization
item.description: Unrest broke out in parts of France as students, trade unionists and Yellow Vest activists took to the streets to protest high prices and inequality. Police arrested over 1,000 people amid chaotic scenes.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
item.description: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

item.title: [DW] What Earth's sixth mass extinction event means for humans
item.description: Human activity is driving plants and animals to extinction at an unprecedented rate. As countries meet in Armenia to discuss ways to reverse nature loss, DW reveals how declining biodiversity is already harming people.
